title: Adaptive route-lineage capture & compressed decision logs
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Our current routing telemetry produces verbose per-request decision payloads that balloon storage and make SLO-aligned debugging expensive. We need high-fidelity lineage for problematic requests (region choice, tier routing decision, fallback model variant selected and why) while keeping overall ingestion and retention costs bounded.

Goal: Implement an adaptive capture mechanism that records full route-lineage envelopes only for sampled triggers (SLO violation candidates, low-confidence model outputs, or explicit debug flags). For non-sampled requests produce compact compressed envelopes and aggregated micro-metrics per route hop. This preserves debugging signal for incidents while reducing storage and privacy exposure.

Proposal:
1) Introduce a small, versioned "route-lineage envelope" format (v1) that includes: route_policy_id, timestamps at each routing stage, chosen tier/model id, rationale code (cache miss / cost-fallback / region-preference), and an optional base64-encoded short KV snapshot when sampled.
2) Implement adaptive sampling rules in the router:
   - Always-sample when request triggers SLA-latency > 90th pct or error-rate threshold.
   - Probabilistic sample for cold-starts and new model variants (configurable rate).
   - Allow explicit per-request debug token to force sampling.
3) For non-sampled requests write a compact telemetry record: hashed route_policy_id, outcome code, latency bucket, and a small bloom-like tagset representing hops touched. These records are optimized for columnar ingestion.
4) Compression & retention: sampled envelopes stored compressed (lz4 + delta-encoding) with 90-day retention; compact records retained 365 days.
5) Privacy: redact PII in envelopes and hash tenant identifiers with per-tenant salts stored in KMS.

Trade-offs:
- Pros: preserves deep debugging for incidents while controlling cost; enables reconstructable lineage for RCA; reduces long-tail storage needs.
- Cons: additional complexity in router logic; introduces per-tenant key management; possible edge cases where sampled/non-sampled mix makes replay harder — mitigated by deterministic hashing and request-id sticky sampling.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria key.
comments: 2026-02-11 | Sofia Patel: Drafted scope and initial design. Spoke with Runtime infra (Miguel) about feasible envelope size budget (~2KB for sampled, ~180B for compact).
2026-02-18 | Ravi Menon: Implementation plan accepted in eng sync. Dependency: needs a small schema registry entry for route-lineage-v1 and KMS support for tenant salt discovery (ticket ENG-44112).

2026-02-25 | Priya Desai (Observability): Reviewed storage plan — suggested lz4 compression and using existing parquet pipeline for compact records. Also suggested adding a dedicated index column for sampled=true to speed incident queries.

2026-03-02 | Security (Arjun Rao): Reviewed privacy approach; requested explicit PII redaction list and threat model note. Security review required before release. See Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Route+Lineage+Privacy

2026-03-05 | Ravi Menon: PoC implemented: router attaches envelope_id and stores sampled payload to s3-compatible bucket; compact records emitted to observability pipeline. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4821

2026-03-09 | QA (Helena Brooks): Smoke tests passed for sampling triggers; hitting an edge case where probabilistic sampler and forced debug token conflict — added deterministic override rule in config. Added unit tests for envelope serialization.
acceptance_criteria: Router emits route-lineage envelopes in v1 format when sampling triggers are hit and writes compact records otherwise.
Sampled envelopes compressed and retrievable via observability console links in incident view.
Compact records ingestable into existing columnar pipeline and queryable in <30s for 7-day windows.
PII redaction and tenant-salted hashing validated by security review and automated tests.
Documentation added: Confluence design doc, runbook for incident snapshot extraction, and console support for toggling per-request debug tokens.
